UnpopularPolicies of Aurangzeb
Accordingto somehistorians,some oftheAurangzeb's policies caused serious discontent
among the Muslims and the non-Muslims alike. These policies were:
Financial difficulties of the empire increased due to the policy of long-drawn wars
of Aurangzeb.He imposed heavy taxes including war tax on the common'people
which were beyond their means.The wealth of the empire was reduced because
farming,trade and industry were not flourishing allacross India.
Aurangzebwantedtounitethe Subcontinentunder his own politico-religious will
whichcaused problemsforhisrule.Forinstance,Aurangzebbroughtback Jizyatax
on Hindus and other non-Muslims which was abolished by Akbar.Hindus were not
happy at having to pay Jizya.
NoteforTeachers
Inform the students that the Marathas were Hindu warriors from the Deccan
located in the south of India.They caused Aurangzeb and his successors many
difficulties as they invaded Mughal lands. They signed a peace treaty with
Aurangzebin 1665 AD, but it dissolved soon after.Laterin 1681AD, the Marathas
became so troublesome that Aurangzeb moved to Deccan to fight against them.
However Aurangzeb could nevereliminate them completely
